overview: The data layer is the ingestion and caching tier of the volforecast pipeline: it turns Goldman internal market data services into per-symbol parquet caches and model-ready tensors that every downstream feature layer and model consumes. Three services feed it. Chunk Store (via pytickclient) supplies raw L1 trade and quote ticks and server-side aggregated bars for the 34-symbol universe; TSDB (the eqpad_ namespace, via gs_quant_internal TSDBSymbol) supplies daily OHLCV, treasury, FX, commodity, VIX and SPX series; Marquee's EDRVOL_PERCENT dataset supplies the SPX implied volatility surface. From ticks, measures.py computes the daily realized volatility panel: realized variance from squared 5 minute returns, jump-robust bipower variation, the BNS z-test that splits RV into continuous and jump components, Patton-Sheppard semivariances, realized quarticity, and a Parzen realized kernel with a noise gap proxy for microstructure noise. rv_panel.py orchestrates calendar-aware, checkpointed streaming fetch and compute, writing per-symbol panels to data/raw/ticks/. micro.py builds 10 second signed-volume bars with BVC trade classification, daily VPIN and order-flow aggregates (data/raw/micro/) plus flat bar sequences (data/raw/micro/sequences/), which sequence_cache.py pre-stacks into padded (n_dates, max_bars, n_features) float32 tensors cached as .pt files under data/processed/sequences/ so LSTM and TCN training is pure tensor ops; a train-dates-only normaliser prevents leakage. iv_ingest.py and iv_features.py assemble the SPX IV panel (ATM 1m and 3m, 25 delta wings, skew, VIX) and derive one-day-shifted causal features such as the variance risk premium, using a HAR-CJ 22 day forecast as the conditional expectation. Specialist modules reconstruct 0DTE variance swap strikes with the CBOE discrete formula (varswap_reconstruct, gsvivs_kvar, spx_allday_vols). Note for readers: the restore is missing volforecast/constants.py, volforecast/data/edrvol.py and volforecast/models/har_family.py, all imported by files in this layer.

modules.role: Ingestion, estimator, and cache layer for the vol forecasting pipeline. Fetches ticks and bars from Chunk Store (pytickclient), daily and cross-asset series from TSDB, and the SPX IV surface from Marquee EDRVOL_PERCENT, then computes daily realized volatility measures (RV, bipower variation, jump tests, semivariances, realized kernel) and microstructure aggregates (VPIN, order flow imbalance). Everything is persisted as per-symbol parquet caches under data/raw/ with atomic temp-file-then-rename writes and merge-never-discard semantics. It feeds the feature layers (har_core, asymmetry, IV features) and, through sequence_cache.py, the deep learning models with padded per-day tensors. A separate cluster of files (gsvivs_kvar, varswap_reconstruct, spx_allday_vols) applies the CBOE discrete variance swap formula to option strips for 0DTE Kvar analysis.

modules.role: paths.py anchors every cache location to the repo root (found via AGENTS.md or vol.cmd marker files) so caches resolve correctly regardless of CWD. It defines the canonical data/raw/ layout: ticks/ for daily RV panels, iv/ for options-implied data, ohlcv/ for daily prices, micro/ and micro/sequences/ for microstructure aggregates and 10s bar sequences, cross_asset/ and correlation/ for the remaining layers, plus data/processed/ for feature panels and sequence tensors. Deprecated aliases keep old call sites working after the directory migration.

claims.text: The daily realized variance measure is the plain sum of squared intraday returns with no mean subtraction, following Andersen et al. 2003.
claims.quote: RV_t = sum(r_{t,i}^2).  No mean subtraction (Andersen et al. 2003).

claims.text: Bipower variation, computed as (pi/2) times the sum of adjacent absolute return products, gives a jump-robust estimate of integrated variance per Barndorff-Nielsen and Shephard 2004.
claims.quote:
BPV = (pi/2) * sum(|r_i| * |r_{i-1}|) for i = 2, ..., N.
    BPV is robust to jumps and estimates integrated variance

claims.text: Good and bad volatility come from Patton and Sheppard 2015 realized semivariances, with RS+ using the >= 0 convention so that RS+ plus RS- always equals RV as an exhaustive partition.
claims.quote:
RS+ = sum(r_i^2 * I(r_i >= 0))
    RS- = sum(r_i^2 * I(r_i < 0))
    Follows Patton & Sheppard (2015): RS+ uses >= 0 so that
    RS+ + RS- = RV always holds (exhaustive partition).

claims.text: Days with statistically significant jumps are flagged by the Barndorff-Nielsen and Shephard 2006 z-test, Z_BNS = (RV - BPV) / sqrt(theta * RTQ / n) with theta approximately 0.609.
claims.quote:
Z_BNS = (RV - BPV) / sqrt(theta * RTQ / n)
    where theta = (pi^2/4 + pi - 5) approx 0.6090.

claims.text: Realized variance is decomposed into a jump component J^2 = max(RV - BPV, 0) gated by the jump indicator and a continuous component C = RV - J, the raw inputs for HAR-CJ style models.
claims.quote:
J^2 = max(RV - BPV, 0) * jump_indicator.
    C = RV - J (continuous variation = total minus jumps).

claims.text: The realized kernel estimator weights return autocovariances with a flat-top Parzen kernel (Barndorff-Nielsen, Hansen, Lunde and Shephard 2008) to stay consistent under microstructure noise, achieving the optimal n^(-1/5) MSE rate.
claims.quote:
RK_t = sum_{h=-H}^{H} k(h/(H+1)) * gamma_hat_h
    Uses the flat-top Parzen kernel (Barndorff-Nielsen, Hansen, Lunde &
    Shephard 2008, Econometrica). Achieves the optimal n^{-1/5} MSE rate.

claims.text: The fast 'bars' ingestion mode computes the full daily RV measure set from roughly 78 pre-aggregated 5 minute bars instead of millions of raw ticks, at the cost of skipping the realized kernel and noise gap which need tick-level prices.
claims.quote:
Equivalent to compute_daily_rv_from_ticks() but operates on ~78 bars
    instead of millions of raw ticks. Does NOT compute realized_kernel or
    noise_gap (those require tick-level data).

claims.text: The RV panel builder is a streaming batch pipeline (trading calendar, batched tick fetch, daily RV computation, checkpoint) whose peak memory is bounded to one sub-batch of tick data at a time.
claims.quote:
Orchestrates: trading calendar -> batch-fetch ticks -> compute daily RV -> cache.
  For each sub-batch: fetch -> compute (optionally parallel) -> checkpoint -> release.
  Peak memory is bounded to one sub-batch of tick data at a time.

claims.text: Raw tick data comes from Chunk Store via pytickclient: L1 trades and quotes for all 34 symbols plus L2 order book depth for the E-mini S&P 500 future, the foundation for RV at any sampling frequency.
claims.quote:
Provides functions to fetch L1 trade/quote data for all 34 symbols and
L2 order book depth data for E-mini S&P 500. Raw tick data is the
foundation for computing realized volatility measures at arbitrary
frequencies (5-min, 1-min, tick-by-tick).

claims.text: TSDB supplies the daily cross-asset series used for feature construction: OHLCV, treasury yields, FX rates, commodity prices, VIX, VIX futures term structure, and SPX index levels.
claims.quote:
Provides functions to fetch daily OHLCV data, treasury yields,
FX rates, commodity prices, VIX, VIX futures, and SPX index data
used for cross-asset feature construction.

claims.text: TSDB only publishes an adjusted close, so ohlcv.py derives split-adjusted open, high, and low by scaling raw prices with the corporate-action factor adj_close / raw_close, while volume stays unadjusted.
claims.quote:
TSDB only provides adjusted close (close.adj.allincdiv). We derive
    adjusted open/high/low by applying the same corporate-action factor:
        adj_price = raw_price * (adj_close / raw_close)

claims.text: micro.py ingests server-classified tick data into 10 second signed-volume bars, producing both daily microstructure aggregates (signed volume ratio, VPIN, order flow imbalance) and per-bar sequences for the deep learning models, cached under data/raw/micro/.
claims.quote:
Fetches tick data with server-side LeeReadySumVolume trade classification,
aggregates into 10-second signed-volume bars, then produces:
  1. Daily aggregates (signed_volume_ratio, vpin, ofi) → data/raw/micro/{SYM}.parquet
  2. 10-second bar sequences (for LSTM/TCN) → data/raw/micro/sequences/{SYM}.parquet

claims.text: VPIN is computed over volume-time buckets as the mean absolute buy-sell volume imbalance per bucket, following Easley, Lopez de Prado and O'Hara 2012.
claims.quote:
Reference: Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012), Eq. 1.
    VPIN = (1/n) * Σ |V^B_i - V^S_i| / V_bucket

claims.text: Every IV-derived feature is shifted by one day before use, so the feature value at time t only reflects information available at market close t-1.
claims.quote:
All features are shifted by 1 day to enforce causality: the feature
    value at time t uses only information available at market close t-1.

claims.text: The variance risk premium feature is squared ATM implied volatility minus a conditional expectation of future RV, where the expectation is a HAR-CJ 22 day ahead forecast in the spirit of Bollerslev et al. 2009.
claims.quote:
# VRP = IV^2 - E_t[RV_{t+1:t+22}]
    # Use HAR-CJ h=22 forecast as the conditional expectation (Bollerslev et al. 2009).

claims.text: sequence_cache.py pre-stacks the per-symbol 10 second bar parquets into a single zero-padded tensor of shape (n_dates, max_bars, n_features) so LSTM and TCN training runs as pure GPU tensor ops with no pandas or parquet overhead.
claims.quote:
Pre-stacks the per-symbol 10s bar parquets under ``data/raw/micro/sequences/``
into a single padded tensor of shape ``(n_dates, max_bars, n_features)`` so
the training loop is pure GPU tensor ops with no pandas / parquet overhead.

claims.text: The DeepVol-style multi-day builder concatenates 20 trading days of 5 minute bars into 1,560-timestep sequences ordered oldest to newest so causal convolutions see the correct time flow.
claims.quote:
For the DeepVol paper architecture: lookback_days=20 → 20×78=1,560
    timesteps per sequence.  Each sequence is ordered oldest→newest

claims.text: Sequence normalisation statistics are fit only on valid bars from training dates, with pad rows and validation and test dates excluded, so there is zero leakage into the normaliser.
claims.quote:
Pad rows (beyond ``lengths[i]``) and non-training dates are excluded so
    there is zero leakage from validation / test folds into the normaliser.

glossary.definition: Sum of squared intraday returns over a trading day, the model target throughout the project; computed with no mean subtraction.
Jump-robust estimator of integrated variance built from products of adjacent absolute returns, scaled by pi/2.
The parts of RV coming from positive versus negative returns; their difference is the signed jump measure used for good and bad volatility features.
Noise-robust integrated variance estimator that weights return autocovariances with a flat-top Parzen kernel.
(RK - RV_5min) / RV_5min, a liquidity and microstructure-noise intensity proxy comparing the kernel estimate to 5 minute RV.
Volume-Synchronized Probability of Informed Trading: mean absolute buy-sell imbalance across equal-volume buckets, per Easley, Lopez de Prado and O'Hara 2012.
Bulk Volume Classification via the tick rule: a bar's volume counts as buy-initiated if close is above open, sell-initiated if below, split evenly if flat.
GS internal Time Series Database, queried through gs_quant_internal TSDBSymbol with eqpad_ prefixed symbols; source of daily OHLCV and cross-asset series.
GS internal tick store accessed via pytickclient, supplying L1 trades and quotes and server-side aggregated bars.
Marquee dataset carrying the SPX implied volatility surface by tenor and relative strike, the raw input for options-implied features.
Variance risk premium: ATM implied variance minus a conditional expectation of future realized variance, here a HAR-CJ 22 day forecast.
The variance swap strike; gsvivs_kvar.py recovers the exact execution Kvar sold each day by applying the CBOE discrete variance swap formula to option fill prices.
